- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the fall; increase downward bias by 2–3% to align with sentiment-driven bearish momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7); add a small upward bias (1–2%) to counteract mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model lags in adjusting; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture sentiment shift.
- In high volatility periods (e.g., sentiment swings >0.3), model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast volatility by 10–15% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
